rationale: The corrected sparse run (receipt fde347cf379748d7bd0a3b6b8deb1d8c) confirms the trim defect: with all three configured nodes at accepted 3 and decided 3, the leader rejected trim(Some(2)) with NotAllDecided(0) and trim(None) left compacted at 0. This update re-submits the asserted compaction/progress account and the executed fact, and marks the question explained; the previous turn's draft was overwritten by a housekeeping submission before it reached the controller.

knowledge.statement: On the executed three-node configuration {1,2,5} with three decided entries and all_accepted_min 3, trim(Some(2)) returned NotAllDecided(0), the compacted index stayed 0, and a following trim(None) also left the compacted index at 0 while returning Ok.
knowledge.conditions: Three OmniPaxos instances pids 1, 2 and 5, ClusterConfig {configuration_id:1, nodes:[1,2,5]}, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, no snapshots; node 1 elected with try_become_leader; three entries appended and fully delivered so every node reports decided 3 and accepted 3.

interpretations.rationale: The executed run shows the wrong minimum being used for trim. Receipt fde347cf379748d7bd0a3b6b8deb1d8c ran sparse_pids_block_automatic_trim (exit 0, test passed). Event 0 (setup) records three configured nodes {1,2,5}, decided 3 and all_accepted_min 3, so every configured server has accepted index 3. Event 1 (trim_result) records requested 2, all_accepted_min 3, trim_ok false, error_min 0, compacted_after_some 0, none_ok true and compacted_after_none 0: an index accepted by all configured nodes is rejected with NotAllDecided(0), and the default trim compacts nothing. The source explains it: LeaderState::with allocates accepted_indexes with one slot per pid up to the largest pid, initialized to 0; pids 3 and 4 are absent from the configuration, so their slots are never updated, and get_min_all_accepted_idx returns the minimum over the whole vector, which is 0. SequencePaxos::trim uses that minimum both as the default trim index and as the bound for an explicit index, so automatic trim cannot progress for any configuration with absent pids below the maximum. The result is that the trim compaction path is unusable in such configurations and storage grows unless the user compacts another way (trim only affects local storage and forwarded Compaction messages, so decision safety and agreement are unaffected; snapshot(Some(idx)) does not consult the minimum and remains an alternative). The declared comparison reported unknown only because the admission alias setup lacked the requested identity field used by the comparison; both event operands were fully observed.
counterevidence: Configurations with contiguous pids from 1 to the maximum have no absent slots, so the minimum is the true minimum and trim works; the defect is limited to configurations with gaps below the largest pid.
trim only affects local storage plus the forwarded compaction message, so it does not affect decision values, agreement or safety.
The snapshot path does not use the minimum accepted index, so a user can still compact with snapshot; the broken surface is the trim API and any automatic trimming built on it.
limitations: One sparse layout ({1,2,5}), majority quorum, unit batch size, memory storage and no snapshots; reconfiguration and crash recovery are unexercised.
The comparison outcome is unknown for admission-identity reasons; the asserted defect rests on the parsed event operands, which are complete.
No forward-compaction failure was observed on followers; the probe only measures the leader's trim decision and its local compacted index.
